title: toolry
why: Useful for remembering complex commands that aren't used frequently and have complex syntax.
Define commands in small TypeScript plugin files, wire them together with a shell alias, and get a fully interactive, categorised CLI with zero boilerplate.

sections.title: How to set it up
body: # Add a shell alias (~/.bashrc or similar)
alias tools="pnpx toolry ~/.toolry/*.ts" # If using ts you need tsx or bun or a new enough node version (24+) that can directly run ts files
Now `tools` anywhere gives you a beautiful interactive menu.

sections.title: Writing a plugin
body: A plugin is any `.ts` or `.js` file that exports one or more tools via `defineTool` / `defineTools`.
fresh: { type: "boolean", description: "Drop all tables first?" },
That's it. Full autocomplete on `args` and `run`. Under 20 lines.
